etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin concīsus (“cut short”), from concīdere (“cut to pieces”), from caedēre (“to cut, to strike down”).

definitions.definition: Brief, yet including all important information

quote.citation: 1856, Lady Emmeline Charlotte E. Stuart Wortley, The Sweet South, page 56:
quote.text: This, however, must refer solely to the length; unfortunately they were far too broad in proportion (the fault I have always observed in them). This directly gives a slightly hoofish look, as in the concise Chinese feet.

definitions.definition: (India, transitive) To make concise; to abridge or summarize.
